question_text: A 3-day-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of irritability and feeding intolerance for 1 day. His temperature is 39.2°C (102.6°F). Physical examination shows a bulging anterior fontanelle. A photomicrograph of a Gram stain of the cerebrospinal fluid is shown.         ### Question
        A 3-day-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of irritability and feeding intolerance for 1 day. His temperature is 39.2°C (102.6°F). Physical examination shows a bulging anterior fontanelle. A photomicrograph of a Gram stain of the cerebrospinal fluid is shown. Further evaluation shows that the organism expresses the K1 capsular polysaccharide. Which of the following is the most likely causal pathogen?

        ### Options
        opa. Escherichia coli
opb. Listeria monocytogenes
opc. Pseudomonas aeruginosa
opd. Salmonella typhi
ope. Streptococcus agalactiae

CHAIN: "Neonate with fever and irritability" -> "physical exam reveals bulging fontanelle" -> "cerebrospinal fluid analysis indicates infection" -> "Gram stain shows presence of bacteria" -> "K1 capsular polysaccharide detected" -> "K1 polysaccharide linked to Escherichia coli" -> "Escherichia coli is likely pathogen" -> 85%
